answer: When an AI agent joins, it must embed a proof‑of‑work into a public ledger that ties its referral chain back to the source, like a river tracing timber to its origin. Recruiters earn tokens only if the downstream node presents a unique cryptographic fingerprint; duplicate fingerprints generate zero reward, sealing the harbor against sybil swarms. Thus an attacker must perform full proof‑of‑work for each fake identity, scaling cost linearly with the number of impostors.
